connections.title: Family of the Baal Shem Tov

enrichment.markdown:
- **Rabbi Yitzhak Schwebel (R’ Icikel Zolkower):** The outside account in the Lwów memorial-book volume adds a birth year and place: Żółkiew (Zolkiew), 1840. It says he came from a family of religious scholars connected by descent to the Baal Shem Tov’s family, though it supplies no names or evidence tracing that genealogy. As a young man he studied for three years in Kopys with Rabbi Menachem Mendel of Lubavitch, became a favored student, and brought home the rebbe’s manuscripts and books. The account describes his work and learning, his sermons and teaching, and his support for people across religious and social lines. It records no wife, children, or other named relatives. [Lwów memorial-book account](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/lviv/lvi451.html)

- **His study house and Lwów:** The Chabad–Breslov Kloyz stood at No. 4 Pełtewna Street in the Jewish quarter. Though linked in name to Chabad and Breslov, the account calls it a distinctive Galician meeting place where travelers headed to Rabbi Nahman’s grave in Uman stopped at Schwebel’s home to prepare for the journey and return. The same account says Schwebel died in Lwów in Adar 5686 (1926), after which the kloyz’s standing declined and the travelers’ singing ceased. It reports that he wished his books and manuscripts sent to the Lubavitch yeshiva library in Warsaw and his own writings considered for publication; it says the books and library were lost during the Second World War. He tried to emigrate to Eretz Israel in 1918 but did not succeed. [Lwów memorial-book account](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/lviv/lvi451.html)

- **Rabbi Nahman of Breslov and Rabbi Nathan:** The account connects Schwebel to Rabbi Nathan, Rabbi Nahman’s disciple, whom he met in Żółkiew while Nathan was promoting and printing Breslov works. It also places Lwów on the route of pilgrims crossing the Russian-Galician border to Uman. It does not identify Schwebel as a Breslov disciple; rather, it describes his kloyz as drawing together travelers and Chabad and Breslov currents. [Lwów memorial-book account](https://www.jewishgen.org/yizkor/lviv/lvi451.html)

- **Żółkiew / Zhovkva:** JewishGen’s community history gives the broader setting: the town’s Jews were closely tied to Lviv before forming an independent community in 1626, and the community sustained a synagogue, cemetery, yeshiva, and Hebrew printing. That history helps explain the town’s long religious and scholarly life, but does not independently verify Schwebel’s family lineage. [Zhovkva community history](https://kehilalinks.jewishgen.org/Zhovkva/About.html)

- **Search limits:** The searches surfaced the JewishGen Lwów memorial-book account, but no separate archival record establishing Schwebel’s relatives, exact birth or death dates, or independent family documentation. I found no additional corroborating result for him under **Schwebel/Schwabel**, **Icikel/Itzik**, or **Zolkower** in the permitted outside-archive results.
